original_question: Can one prove a lower bound for computing X_alpha in the same two-coordinate unitary-step model that is stronger than Omega(alpha n log n), possibly by choosing a nontrivial unitary representation Psi of U(n), composing the entropy-style potential Phi with Psi, and in particular exploiting the order-k determinant representation Psi_det^k(U) whose (I, J) entry is det U_{I,J}?
target_in_paper: Section 2.2, "Stronger improvements?"—the open problem asking whether one can prove a lower bound for computing X_α that is stronger than the Ω(α n log n) bound from Section 2.1, with the explicitly suggested representation-theoretic route of replacing Φ by Φ∘Ψ. The determinant/minor representation mentioned in your draft matches the specific representation proposed there. The paper does not package this as a numbered conjecture; the nearest official formulation is this Section 2.2 question, read together with Section 2, Section 2.1, and the nearby conjectural discussion in footnote 1.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact object X_α, the same two-coordinate unitary-step computational model, the currently proved Ω(α n log n) lower bound from the paper, and the paper’s proposed strategy of using a nontrivial unitary representation Ψ and the composed potential Φ∘Ψ. It also captures the paper’s specific interest in determinant/minor-type representations.
missing_details: The matrix being computed is 2n×2n, not n×n: X_α acts on C^{2n}.
The ambient field is C, and the group under discussion is the unitary group of the relevant dimension (for X_α, naturally U(2n), or U(N) with N=2n).
F must be defined explicitly as the normalized n×n Fourier matrix, and X_α is built from it via G = [[0, F], [-F^*, 0]] and X_α = (cos α)I_{2n} + (sin α)G.

The computational model should be stated precisely: one seeks a factorization X_α = R_m ... R_1 where each R_t is unitary and equals the identity except on a single 2×2 unitary block, i.e. one arbitrary two-coordinate unitary gate per step, with no extra memory.

The current best lower bound from the paper is not just 'entropy-style' in general; it is specifically the Section 2.1 bound Ω(α n log n), improving the more basic Ω(α^2 n log n) bound from Section 2.
The relevant parameter regime is small real α (the paper discusses α in the small-angle regime, e.g. α in (0, π/4), and α may depend on n).
The asymptotic question should specify the complexity measure m as a function of n and α, typically as n→∞ with α=α(n).

If the determinant representation is mentioned, it should be defined precisely: for k-subsets I,J of [2n], (Ψ_det^k(U))_{I,J} = det(U_{I,J}), where U_{I,J} is the k×k submatrix with row set I and column set J.
Your draft does not mention the paper’s nearby stronger conjectural target from footnote 1, namely Ω((n log n)/log(1/α)), which is the concrete benchmark motivating 'stronger than Ω(α n log n)'.

The draft does not mention the paper’s note that even restricted small-α cases are already interesting, so the problem should remain narrowly about X_α rather than drifting to a broader Fourier-transform lower-bound program.
refined_question: Let F be the normalized n×n discrete Fourier matrix over C, let G := [[0, F], [-F^*, 0]] ∈ C^{2n×2n}, and for a real parameter α define X_α := (cos α)I_{2n} + (sin α)G, so that X_α is unitary and X_{α'}X_α = X_{α+α'}. In the no-extra-memory linear model where computing X_α means factoring X_α = R_m ... R_1 with each R_t a 2n×2n unitary matrix that is the identity except on one 2×2 unitary block (one arbitrary two-coordinate unitary gate per step), can one prove a lower bound on m that is asymptotically stronger than the Ω(α n log n) bound of Section 2.1 for small α=α(n) (for example α∈(0,π/4])? In particular, can one obtain the conjecturally correct Ω((n log n)/log(1/α)) bound, or any super-Ω(α n log n) bound, by replacing the basic entropy potential Φ(U) = -∑_{i,j}|U_{ij}|^2 log |U_{ij}|^2 with Φ∘Ψ for a nontrivial unitary representation Ψ of U(2n), especially the order-k determinant/minor representation defined by (Ψ_det^k(U))_{I,J} = det(U_{I,J}) for k-subsets I,J ⊂ [2n]?
justification: The draft is aimed squarely at the open problem posed in Section 2.2. Section 2 defines G and X_α and explains why the naive entropy argument only gives Ω(α^2 n log n), while Section 2.1 improves this to Ω(α n log n). Section 2.2 then explicitly asks whether one can prove a stronger lower bound than α n log n and proposes exactly the representation-theoretic strategy your draft mentions: choose a unitary representation Ψ and study Φ∘Ψ; the nearby text specifically discusses determinant/minor-based representations. Footnote 1 gives the paper’s concrete conjectural benchmark Ω((n log n)/log(1/α)), and the following subsection emphasizes that even small-α special cases are already nontrivial. So the refined question stays tightly on the paper’s actual X_α problem, while making the model, matrix definitions, ambient group, and determinant representation explicit.
